timeline.event: The Althing assembly first meets at Þingvellir
Erik the Red leads settlers from Iceland to Greenland
timeline.label: c. 985

timeline.event: Leif Erikson's crew reaches North America
timeline.label: c. 1000

timeline.event: Snorri Sturluson is killed at his farm in Reykholt
Icelandic chieftains begin swearing loyalty to Norway's king
Catholic bishop Jón Arason is executed at Skálholt
Barbary corsairs raid the Westman Islands and carry off captives
The Laki fissure eruption begins, bringing famine
The Althing is abolished by royal decree
King Christian IX grants Iceland its first constitution
Iceland becomes a sovereign kingdom in union with Denmark

places.name: Reykjavík
places.clue: The world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state; its name means 'Smoky Bay', after steam from hot springs.

places.name: Geysir
places.clue: The hot spring that gave English the word 'geyser'; its neighbour Strokkur erupts every few minutes.

places.name: Eyjafjallajökull
places.clue: This ice-capped volcano's 2010 eruption sent an ash cloud over Europe that grounded flights for days.

places.name: Jökulsárlón
places.clue: A glacier lagoon where icebergs broken off Vatnajökull drift past the Ring Road toward the sea.

places.name: Akureyri
places.clue: Often called the capital of North Iceland, this town sits at the head of the long fjord Eyjafjörður.

places.name: Snæfellsjökull
places.clue: In Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth', explorers climb down into this glacier-capped volcano.

places.name: Ísafjörður
places.clue: The largest town in the remote Westfjords, built on a gravel spit in a deep fjord.

places.name: Dettifoss
places.clue: Often called Europe's most powerful waterfall, it thunders into the Jökulsárgljúfur canyon.

places.name: Seyðisfjörður
places.clue: An eastern fjord town of colourful wooden houses, where the car ferry from Denmark docks.

places.name: Laki
places.clue: Its fissure eruption of 1783-84 poisoned livestock and led to a famine that killed about a fifth of Icelanders.

places.name: Reykholt
places.clue: Home of the saga writer Snorri Sturluson, who was killed here in 1241; his stone bathing pool survives.

places.name: Glaumbær
places.clue: A preserved turf-roofed farmhouse in Skagafjörður, now a museum of rural life.
